chapter: Early bands and New Orleans musicians
title: The Triangle Band and the Majana brothers
summary: He played trombone in the Majana brothers' spot-job Triangle Band, quit after a dispute, and talk turns to Sato and Steve Woodrow's wife.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, about the Triangle Band, what was that like? Was that a spot job band?

Yeah, that was strictly a spot job band. That was two Majana brothers, Sato and Tony Majana. And I played trombone with them for a while, then Leon Mello went in, took my place when I quit them. I quit them, we had a little run in about, I went after a job and I got the job and the first night on the job they showed up late and I got balled out for it and I tore them off and I quit the band.
Where did Tony Majana play? Trumpet.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: Sato's still alive, he's still playing with the police band.
Yeah, Sato plays clarinet with the police band.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: I played with him in Monroe. Yeah? Uh huh.

blocks.s: Mrs. Joe Loyacano (wife of Joe Loyacano)
blocks.x: His wife's been real sick and I haven't heard very much of her.
Yeah, well he's married Steve Woodrow's wife. He's married to Steve Woodrow's wife. And Woodrow's dad died, you see. And since Woodrow's dad, he married Woodrow's wife.
